cases.name: Cross-origin clientDataJSON accepted
cases.description: The assertion was sent with clientDataJSON.origin set to an attacker-controlled origin. A compliant RP MUST reject an assertion whose origin does not match an expected origin (WebAuthn §7.2 step 13).

cases.name: Mismatched challenge accepted (replay)
cases.description: The assertion carried a fixed challenge that the server never issued. A compliant RP MUST verify clientDataJSON.challenge equals the challenge it generated (WebAuthn §7.2 step 11). Acceptance indicates the challenge is not bound, enabling replay.
cases.responseExcerpt: {"error": "Client data challenge was not expected challenge"}

cases.name: Signature counter regression accepted
cases.description: The assertion reported signCount=0 after a higher count had been established. An RP that stores signature counts SHOULD treat a non-increasing counter as a sign of a cloned authenticator (WebAuthn §7.2 step 21). Silent acceptance means cloned-credential detection is not in effect.
cases.responseExcerpt: {"error": "Response sign count of 0 was not greater than current count of 2"}

cases.name: Cleared User-Verified flag accepted
cases.description: The assertion was sent with the UV (User Verified) flag bit cleared while the RP requested userVerification=required. A compliant RP MUST verify the UV bit is set when it requires user verification (WebAuthn §7.2 step 17).
cases.responseExcerpt: Mutation not meaningful for the observed baseline policy.

cases.name: "none" attestation accepted where attestation was requested
cases.description: Registration was completed with fmt="none" and a zero AAGUID although the RP requested a non-none attestation. If the RP relies on attestation for authenticator provenance, it MUST validate the attestation statement rather than accept "none".
cases.responseExcerpt: Mutation not meaningful for the observed baseline policy.

cases.name: Assertion with unregistered credential ID accepted
cases.description: The assertion was signed by a freshly generated credential whose ID was never registered for this user. A compliant RP MUST look up the credential by ID and verify the signature against the stored public key (WebAuthn §7.2 steps 3 & 16). Acceptance indicates the credential is not bound to the account.
